{"id":"JMAP-0x0q.48","title":"DID refresh only on key absence, 60 s limit","description":"Oracle: jmap-chat-spec 6bcd9d8 (quoted text). Mapped by wf_6712c4f8-c2b.

[did-cid] Refresh only on key absence, rate-limited to once per 60 s per DID
Spec (b6028b3): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did-00.md L233 @6bcd9d8: "If the key that verified a request signature is not in the `authentication` verification relationship of the cached DID Document ({{did-verification}}), the server MUST resolve the DID again, bypassing its cache, before failing the verification. A server SHOULD NOT resolve one DID again for this reason more often than once every 60 seconds; a request that arrives within that interval and whose signing key is absent from the cached DID Document fails the verification."
Code: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/did_auth.rs:22-28, 74-79, 152-157 (RefreshRequired on UnknownKey OR BadSignature against a Cached document); crate-jmap-did-resolver/src/lib.rs:23-35 (module doc quotes removed 'signature verification against that cached document fails'); crate-jmap-did-resolver/src/lib.rs:299-314 (Resolver::refresh: drops the entry and refetches unconditionally; no per-DID last-forced-refresh record); crate-jmap-did-resolver/tests/resolver.rs:329-351 (oracle quotes removed L243/L248 text); crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/did_auth.rs:260-345 (rotated_key..., bad_signature_against_cached_document_requires_refresh, etc.)
Now: A Cached document whose keys fail with UnknownKey or BadSignature yields RefreshRequired, and the caller calls Resolver::refresh, which always refetches. There is no 60 s limiter. Because refresh first removes the entry, a peer that keeps sending requests signed by a key absent from the document triggers an upstream fetch on every request.
Change: (a) The only refresh trigger is 'signing key not in the cached document's authentication relationship'. BadSignature can no longer reach this code, because the signature is verified against peerSigningKeys first. Drop it from RefreshRequired (whose payload Rejection then goes away). (b) Add a per-DID forced-refresh limiter, ideally in jmap-did-resolver to keep chat-server I/O-free per the decision recorded in commit a1faa4c7. Record the Instant of the last forced refresh per DID, kept separately from the cache entry so removing the entry does not reset it. Within 60 s, refresh must not refetch: it returns the still-cached document, or a distinct error, and the caller fails the verification. Use the existing with_clock for tests. (c) Rewrite the resolver and did_auth caching docs and test oracles to L233.
Verifier correction: As proposed, but treat the 60 s per-DID limit as SHOULD-level default behavior: on by default, with the interval configurable. Record it outside the cache entry, so that remove() does not reset it. Within the interval, the caller fails the verification and does not refetch.
